extracted.intended_audience: Public housing agencies (PHAs), owners of federally assisted housing, Section 8 administrators, and applicants for HUD grants/assistance
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards in 24 CFR Part 5 governing screening, admission prohibitions, eviction authority, access to criminal and sex-offender records, records management, and HUD grant application requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on changing fiscal years
rubrics_metrics.description: PHAs listed in paragraphs (a)(1) and (a)(2) will not be allowed to change their fiscal years for their first three full fiscal years following October 1, 1998.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to allow for a period of consistent assessment of financial reports submitted to HUD under this subpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility for submission of financial report
rubrics_metrics.description: The responsibility for submission of the financial report due to HUD under this section rests with the individuals and entities listed in paragraph (a) of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies which persons/entities are accountable for filing financial reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage of this subpart
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are the owner of federally assisted housing, your federally assisted housing is covered, except as provided in paragraphs (b) or (c) (exclusions for public housing, tenant-based Section 8, certain Rural Housing Administration programs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies which programs and owners are subject to the requirements in this subpart and points to where similar provisions apply for excluded programs (parts 960, 966, 982, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to screen applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: You are authorized to screen applicants for the programs covered by this part. The provisions implement statutory directives that either require or permit action to deny admission under certain circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulation does not constrain an owner's or PHA's authority to screen out applicants they determine unsuitable under their standards for admission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to terminate tenancy
rubrics_metrics.description: You are authorized to terminate tenancy of tenants, in accordance with your leases and landlord-tenant law for the programs covered by this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisions implement statutory directives that require or permit termination under certain circumstances; you retain authority to terminate tenancy on any other authorized basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretion in screening and eviction actions
rubrics_metrics.description: If the law/regulation permit but do not require action, you may take or not take action in accordance with your standards; you may consider all circumstances relevant to a particular case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerated factors to consider include: (1) seriousness of offending action; (2) effect on the community of denial/termination; (3) extent of leaseholder participation; (4) effect on household members not involved; (5) demand for assisted housing by compliant families; (6) extent to which leaseholder showed personal responsibility and steps to prevent/mitigate; (7) effect on program integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of culpable household member
rubrics_metrics.description: You may require an applicant (or tenant) to exclude a household member in order to be admitted to the housing program (or continue to reside), where that household member has participated in or been culpable for action or failure to act that warrants denial or termination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an available remedy to admit/retain households by excluding the culpable individual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of rehabilitation
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining whether to deny admission or terminate tenancy for illegal drug use or alcohol abuse by a household member who is no longer engaged in such behavior, you may consider whether the household member is participating in or has successfully completed a supervised drug or alcohol rehabilitation program or has otherwise been rehabilitated successfully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may require evidence of current participation or successful completion of a supervised program; unless rehabilitation is an element of eligibility that must be considered, you may choose not to consider rehabilitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lengthening statutory prohibition periods
rubrics_metrics.description: If a statute requires that you prohibit admission of persons for a prescribed period after disqualifying behavior, you may apply that prohibition for a longer period of time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits owners/PHAs to adopt more restrictive time periods than statute minimums where allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nondiscrimination limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Your admission and eviction actions must be consistent with fair housing and equal opportunity provisions of § 5.105.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All screening/eviction decisions must comply with nondiscrimination and HUD Equal Access requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: currently engaging in
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Currently engaging in' with respect to illegal drug use or other criminal activity means that the individual has engaged in the behavior recently enough to justify a reasonable belief that the individual's behavior is current.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a temporal standard for assessing whether behavior counts as current.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: owner and responsible entity
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner = owner of federally assisted housing. Responsible entity = for certain programs the PHA administering the program under an Annual Contributions Contract with HUD; for other programs the owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies which actor is the 'responsible entity' in various Section 8 and public housing contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory three-year prohibition after eviction for drug-related criminal activity
rubrics_metrics.description: You must prohibit admission of an applicant for three years from the date of eviction if any household member has been evicted from federally assisted housing for drug-related criminal activity, unless exception applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: (1) the evicted household member has successfully completed an approved supervised drug rehabilitation program; or (2) the circumstances leading to eviction no longer exist (e.g., death or imprisonment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards to prohibit admission for current illegal drug use or reasonable cause
rubrics_metrics.description: You must establish standards that prohibit admission if you determine any household member is currently engaging in illegal use of a drug, or you have reasonable cause to believe a household member's illegal use or pattern of illegal use may interfere with health, safety, or right to peaceful enjoyment by other residents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires written standards that identify these bases for denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorization to prohibit admission for certain criminal activities
rubrics_metrics.description: You may prohibit admission if you determine any household member is currently engaging in, or engaged in during a reasonable time before admission decision, drug-related criminal activity, violent criminal activity, other criminal activity that would threaten health/safety/peaceful enjoyment, or other criminal activity threatening health/safety of PHA/owner/employees/contractors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives owners/PHAs discretion to define 'reasonable time' and to deny based on a range of criminal behaviors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable time period before admission
rubrics_metrics.description: You may establish a period before the admission decision during which an applicant must not have engaged in the disqualifying activities specified (reasonable time).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows owners/PHAs to set look-back periods as part of their admission standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration after prior denial with sufficient evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: If you previously denied admission due to household member's criminal history, you may reconsider if you have sufficient evidence that household members are not currently engaged in and have not engaged in such criminal activity during a reasonable period before the admission decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of sufficient evidence: certification by household member that they are not currently engaged and supporting information (probation officer, landlord, neighbors, social service agency, criminal records) which you verify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of admission for lifetime-registered sex offenders
rubrics_metrics.description: You must establish standards that prohibit admission to federally assisted housing if any member of the household is subject to a lifetime registration requirement under a State sex offender registration program; you must perform necessary criminal history background checks in the State where the housing is located and other States where household members resided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References § 5.905 for details on sex-offender record checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of admission for alcohol abusers
rubrics_metrics.description: You must establish standards that prohibit admission if you determine you have reasonable cause to believe a household member's abuse or pattern of abuse of alcohol interferes with health, safety, or right to peaceful enjoyment by other residents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires written standards and a reasonable-cause determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lease requirement: drug-related criminal activity grounds for termination
rubrics_metrics.description: The lease must provide that drug-related criminal activity engaged in on or near the premises by any tenant, household member, guest, or other person under the tenant's control is grounds for you to terminate tenancy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lease must also allow eviction when you determine a household member is illegally using a drug or a pattern of illegal use interferes with health/safety/peaceful enjoyment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lease requirement: termination for criminal activity threatening others
rubrics_metrics.description: The lease must provide that the owner may terminate tenancy for any criminal activity by a covered person that threatens the health, safety, or right to peaceful enjoyment of the premises by other residents or persons residing in the immediate vicinity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also requires lease provision allowing termination if tenant is a fugitive felon or violating probation/parole conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lease requirement: termination for alcohol abusers
rubrics_metrics.description: The lease must provide that you may terminate the tenancy if you determine a household member's abuse or pattern of abuse of alcohol threatens the health, safety, or right to peaceful enjoyment of the premises by other residents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aligns alcohol-abuse eviction authority with drug-related and other criminal eviction provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence standard for eviction based on criminal activity
rubrics_metrics.description: You may terminate tenancy and evict the tenant through judicial action if you determine that the covered person has engaged in the criminal activity, regardless of whether the covered person has been arrested or convicted for such activity and without satisfying a criminal conviction standard of proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eviction can be based on the PHA/owner's determination of engagement in criminal activity rather than criminal conviction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of Subpart J: criminal records and searches
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart J applies to criminal conviction background checks by PHAs that administer Section 8 and public housing when they obtain criminal conviction records from law enforcement agencies under authority of section 6(q) of the 1937 Act to prevent admission of criminals and assist in lease enforcement/eviction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also covers sex offender registration records under statutory authority; excludes other types of searches not provided under this subpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpart J definitions (adult, covered housing, law enforcement agency, owner, responsible entity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines adult (18+ or convicted as adult), covered housing (public housing, project-based and tenant-based Section 8 programs), law enforcement agency (NCIC, police departments, etc.), owner, and responsible entity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies terms used throughout Subpart J to identify who may act and what housing is covered.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHA authority to obtain criminal conviction records
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are a PHA that administers Section 8 and/or public housing, this section authorizes you to obtain criminal conviction records from a law enforcement agency and to use those records to screen applicants and for lease enforcement or eviction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority is limited to purposes and processes set out in the regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent required for criminal conviction records
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain access under this section, the responsible entity must require every applicant family to submit a consent form signed by each adult household member. By signing, adult household members consent that law enforcement may release criminal conviction records to a PHA and that the PHA may use the records in accordance with this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consent form is prerequisite for PHA requests to law enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for law enforcement release of records
rubrics_metrics.description: When law enforcement receives your request, it must promptly release a certified copy of any criminal conviction records concerning the household member in its possession or control; NCIC records must be provided per NCIC procedures; law enforcement may charge a reasonable fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PHAs should expect certified records and possible fees when requesting from agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Owner access to criminal records via PHA
rubrics_metrics.description: If an owner submits a request to the PHA for criminal records concerning an adult household member, the PHA must request the records from law enforcement, determine whether criminal action shown may be a basis for screening/lease enforcement/eviction, notify the owner of whether records were received and of the determination, and generally must not disclose the record content to the owner except as provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owner's request must include signed consent and the owner's standards for prohibiting admission/eviction/lease enforcement; PHA may charge owners reasonable fees for these services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Owner request contents and uses when seeking records
rubrics_metrics.description: An owner's request to the PHA must include a copy of the consent form and the owner's standards for prohibiting admission of drug criminals (§5.854) or other criminals (§5.855), or the owner's standards for eviction/lease enforcement if the purpose is eviction or lease enforcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests must clearly state intended use (screening, eviction, lease enforcement) and supply necessary supporting information; owners may not pass costs onto applicants/tenants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees for PHA-facilitated record requests
rubrics_metrics.description: If an owner requests a PHA to obtain criminal conviction or sex offender registration records, the PHA may charge the owner reasonable fees for making the request and taking other actions; the PHA may require reimbursement of costs including fees charged by law enforcement and administrative costs. The owner may not pass along costs to applicant or tenant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PHAs must account for and may collect costs, but costs cannot be borne by the applicant/tenant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted use of criminal conviction records received by PHA
rubrics_metrics.description: Criminal conviction records received by a PHA may only be used for applicant screening for specified public housing and Section 8 programs, and for lease enforcement and eviction in the limited contexts described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies which program contexts and distinguishes between project-based and tenant-based uses (e.g., records received by a PHA may not be used for lease enforcement/eviction of Section 8 tenant-based assistance recipients).

rubrics_metrics.name: PHA disclosure limits for criminal conviction records
rubrics_metrics.description: A PHA may disclose criminal conviction records received from law enforcement only to PHA officers/employees/authorized representatives with a job-related need or to an owner for use in connection with judicial eviction proceedings to the extent necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure to owners for judicial eviction is allowed only if PHA determined record may be a basis for eviction and owner certifies in writing limited use; PHA may rely on owner's certification and is not responsible for controlling access after disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to dispute criminal record information
rubrics_metrics.description: If a PHA obtains criminal record information showing conviction relevant to screening/lease enforcement/eviction, the PHA must notify the household of the proposed action, provide the subject and the applicant/tenant a copy of the information, and provide an opportunity to dispute accuracy and relevance before denial/eviction/lease enforcement action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opportunity to dispute must be provided prior to adverse action based on the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Records management for criminal conviction records
rubrics_metrics.description: The PHA must establish and implement a system of records management that ensures any criminal record received from a law enforcement agency is maintained confidentially, not misused or improperly disseminated, and destroyed once the purpose for which the record was requested has been accomplished (including expiration of challenge period or final litigation disposition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records management must be consistent with disclosure limitations; destruction requirements apply except for public information or information obtained by a PHA other than under this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties for improper release of information
rubrics_metrics.description: Criminal penalty: misdemeanor conviction and fine up to $5,000 for anyone who knowingly and willfully requests or obtains information under false pretenses or knowingly and willfully discloses such information to an individual not entitled to receive it. Civil liability: PHAs may be held liable for negligent or knowing unauthorized disclosure and affected persons may sue for damages and other relief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Victims may bring suit in district court in various venues; relief may include reasonable attorney's fees and litigation costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHA obligation to obtain sex offender registration information
rubrics_metrics.description: A PHA administering Section 8 or public housing must carry out background checks necessary to determine whether a household member applying for admission is subject to a lifetime sex offender registration requirement under a State program; checks must cover the State where housing is located and States where household members are known to have resided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the PHA requests such information, the State/local agency must promptly provide it and may charge a reasonable fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Owner's request procedure for sex offender registration information
rubrics_metrics.description: An owner may request the PHA obtain sex offender registration information; the PHA must request the information, determine whether it may be a basis for screening/lease enforcement/eviction (based on owner's criteria), and inform the owner of the determination. The request must specify intended use and include addresses and the owner's standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PHA must not disclose sex offender registration information obtained under this section to the owner; owners must include standards consistent with §5.855(c) or §5.858 as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Records management for sex offender registration information
rubrics_metrics.description: The PHA must implement records management ensuring that sex offender registration information received is maintained confidentially, not misused or improperly disseminated, and destroyed once the purpose is accomplished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements do not apply to public information or information obtained by a PHA other than under this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to dispute sex offender registration information
rubrics_metrics.description: If a PHA obtains sex offender registration information showing a household member is subject to a lifetime registration requirement, the PHA must notify the household of the proposed action, provide a copy of the information, and provide an opportunity to dispute accuracy and relevance before denial/eviction/lease enforcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same procedural protections as for criminal conviction records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of Subpart K: application and submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart K applies to all applicants for HUD grants, cooperative agreements, capital fund or operating fund subsidy, capital advance, or other assistance under HUD programs, including formula grant programs, but excluding FHA insurance and loan guarantees not associated with a grant program or award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes who must follow the application, registration, and submission requirements in Subpart K.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unique entity identifier requirement for HUD applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Every application for a new or renewal HUD grant, cooperative agreement, capital/operating subsidy, capital advance, or other assistance must include a unique entity identifier number for the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules for consortiums, sponsors, managing organizations, and exemptions for individuals are specified; HUD will not consider an application complete until a valid unique entity identifier is provided unless OMB grants an exemption.

rubrics_metrics.name: System for Award Management (SAM) registration requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants for HUD financial assistance subject to this subpart are required to register with SAM and have an active registration in SAM in accordance with 2 CFR part 25, appendix A for HUD to obligate funds and for awardees to receive funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Active SAM registration is a prerequisite for HUD fund obligations and awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic submission requirement for grant applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants described under § 5.1001 are required to submit electronic applications or plans for HUD grants and other financial assistance in response to any application HUD places on www.grants.gov/Apply or its successor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The HUD Assistant Secretary or designated official may waive the electronic submission requirement in writing for an applicant on the basis of good cause.
